cleansingStrength.rationale: Strong: lean Sodium Laureth Sulfate #2 / Cocamidopropyl Betaine #3 chassis with minimal counter-signals (Glycerin #5, Hydrolyzed Keratin #6, Guar #7; no refatting lipid, silicone or nonionic buffer) and explicit deep-cleansing intent ('Tiefenreinigung' in name, 'reinigt intensiv', 'Deep-Cleanse-System'). C1's moderate ruling is conditioned on 'no reset/deep-cleansing intent', so it does not apply; the strong anchor's 'clarifying ... architecture whose net effect remains strong after counter-signals' fits the stripped-down formula.
cleansingStrength.counterSignal: Only one anionic route, betaine-buffered - formula alone is the C1 moderate pattern; claims cannot assign cleansing by themselves (3.2).

conditioningLevel.rationale: Low: cleansing-led; light routes only - Glycerin #5, Hydrolyzed Keratin #6, Guar Hydroxypropyltrimonium Chloride #7. No silicone, fatty or lipid route.
conditioningLevel.counterSignal: Guar is relatively early in a short list.

weightPotential.rationale: Low: one light polymer and a protein; no persistent system; strong reset.

focusPrimary.rationale: Clarifying: explicit deep-cleaning/reset product ('Shampoo Tiefenreinigung', 'Befreit das Haar von Styling-Rückständen', 'Deep-Cleanse-System') with compatible lean SLES/betaine architecture (7.2).
focusPrimary.counterSignal: No chelator or second anionic reset route; daily-use claim.
focusPrimary.decisionTrace: Blind: lean SLES/betaine, light conditioning -> clarifying-compatible. Unblind: name 'Tiefenreinigung' -> clarifying.

focusSecondary.rationale: Empty: 'Leichtigkeit und Glanz' is an outcome of the cleansing route (F2); anti-static is not a focus value.

usageRole.rationale: Occasional_reset: product name contains 'Tiefenreinigung' (D1 lexicon), so §9 marks it an explicit deep-cleansing/reset product. The frequent trigger is excluded because cleansing is strong, even though the manufacturer says 'für die tägliche Anwendung geeignet'.
usageRole.counterSignal: Explicit daily-use suitability; directions do not limit frequency.

scalpComfortTarget.rationale: No sensitive/itchy/dry-scalp positioning; Menthol #9 and fragrance are counter-signals.

projection.thicknessRationale: T1 W low, C low: fine ideal, normal ideal, coarse acceptable. T4: W no neighbor; C neighbor moderate keeps coarse acceptable -> no flags.
projection.scalpTargetRationale: Manufacturer body copy says the formula 'entfernt wirksam Styling-Rückstände sowie überschüssiges Fett von Haar und Kopfhaut'. This names the scalp and excess oil (close to E2 'überschüssiger Talg') but describes what is removed in a buildup product 'für alle Haartypen', not a targeted oily-scalp state; E1 grades it low (ambiguous), and low positioning cannot support a target, so S-OILY is not emitted. S-ORDINARY literally requires 'no E2 scalp claim at all', so ordinary is proposed with review_rule_conflict (P0: fail to review). Had oily been accepted, S-OILY's formula gate (strong, W low, C low) would pass.
projection.cleansingIntensityRationale: I1: strong + occasional_reset + clarifying primary -> clarifying (I2: kept; amber in everyday role). I3: neighbor moderate -> regular, equal to the normal bucket's expected regular where clarifying is not -> review_intensity_boundary.
projection.deepCleanserRationale: D1 true ('Tiefenreinigung' in product name, E1 high). D2: strong + clarifying primary + occasional_reset + D1 -> flagged; regular-shampoo rows kept. Confidence = min(cleansing moderate, focus moderate, usage moderate, D1 high) = moderate. If cleansing were moderate, D2 would fail and D3 would raise review_reset_positioning_mismatch instead.
projection.liveComparison: Not evaluated (live rows not in sealed packet).

uncertainties: C1 vs 3.2: C1 makes a SLES/betaine formula moderate only when there is 'no reset/deep-cleansing intent', which lets intent (a claim) move cleansing to strong, while 3.2 says claims may not assign cleansing. For a lean SLES/betaine formula named 'Tiefenreinigung' the standard does not say which wins; chose strong (moderate confidence, neighbor moderate). The choice flips D2 (flagged) vs D3 (mismatch review).
§9 occasional_reset is triggered by the D1 lexicon alone, even when the manufacturer says the product is suitable for daily use; no rule reconciles the two.

E2/E1/S-ORDINARY gap: an oil-removal statement naming the scalp inside a buildup product. S-ORDINARY needs 'no E2 claim at all', S-FAIL covers only formula-gate failure, and E1 'low' blocks the target; no rule says what to project. Resolved: ordinary + review_rule_conflict.
The standard's D2 pattern cites a Balea regular-shampoo record plus a deep-cleanser record; whether that refers to this product cannot be verified from the packet, so the note is 'needs_record'.
